findings: Unpaid_Invoiced_Amount is a formula; do not write it.
Invoice_Edit_Key already exists and is unique on payments and payment allocations.
Payment_Accounting_Status does not exist on Supplier_Pay_Allocations.
Published allocation editing used Invoice_Total over Total_Payable_Amount, cached Amount_Paid for availability, and counted all payment statuses as paid.

model.invoice_total: Main VAT-inclusive amount + additional VAT-inclusive amount - main withholding - additional withholding.
model.total_payable: Invoice_Total + Reimbursable_Expense. Each component uses the existing two-decimal rounding rules.
model.reserved: Current allocations whose payment is not Cancelled.
model.paid: Current allocations whose payment is Paid or Reconciled.
model.settlement_distribution: Existing rebuildSupplierSettlementTotals distributes invoice payments by active Inv_Set_Allocations shares, using payable as denominator; credit notes/refunds retain their negative settlement contribution.
model.payment_editor: Preserves existing behavior: Payment_Amount is the absolute signed net of allocations; omitted invoices remain linked and explicit zero unlinks. The UI now labels the resulting payment total, rather than suggesting an unapplied balance is retained.
model.administrative_states: Cancelled/Rejected invoices and locked/exported/reconciled payments block this editor. Invoice financial statuses derive from paid allocations; payment Accounting_Status is not reset by allocation editing. Settlement states follow the existing rebuild function.
model.fixed_invoice_relationships: Invoice editing retains supplier, primary settlement and the existing settlement set; existing server snapshots reject changed relationships during recovery.
model.related_operations: Payment creation synchronizes prepayments/card purchases and preserves recovery until required links complete. Allocation changes to a payment with accounting entries or linked operations are blocked and directed to the existing correction/undo flow.

changes: Supplier invoice registration rejects cancelled/locked settlements and detects external allocations on incomplete invoices even if cached Amount_Paid is zero.
Invoice editing rejects fractional-cent existing payment allocations; existing tax, withholding, prepayment reservation, payment correction and accounting-entry protections remain in force.
Payment availability and UI totals prefer Total_Payable_Amount, including reimbursables, over legacy invoice totals/formula snapshots.
All allocation-manager validations precede writes; complete paginated reads reject duplicates and read failures; affected settlements include active invoice splits and explicitly removed invoices.
Reconciliation derives paid amounts from live allocation/payment records, updates financial statuses and allocation snapshots, recomputes payment context counts, and never writes the unpaid formula.

General payment creation journals the immutable request before financial writes, uses existing unique keys for payment/allocation inserts, suppresses duplicate workflow calculations, and retains recovery through reconciliation, operation synchronization and UI refresh failures.

Prepayment/card payment routes use immutable operation keys and the same server reconciliation; the prepayment journal migrates session recovery to persistent storage and preserves the original payment date on retries.
Removed unsupported Payment_Accounting_Status writes from payment creation and invoice-deletion payment adjustments.
Capability probes prevent the new widget from invoking an older backend that does not implement validate_only/reconcile_only.
No bulk repair, schema change, published function update, widget upload or ZIP replacement was performed.
deployment_order: Compile and validate the changed Deluge sources in a Zoho test environment first; Node harnesses do not validate the Deluge compiler or actual API behavior.

Upload the widget with payment-save.js loaded before payment-create.js. Coordinate both server create callers: prepayment-workflow.js and operations.js now send operation_key and explicit allocations. Older callers fail closed and must be upgraded.

validation.focused: 217 tests passed together; two additional lost-insert-response tests passed with the 12-test server suite afterward.
validation.full_suite: 550 passed / 562 executed in the full regression run; 12 failures reference missing pre-existing _local CRM source files. Two newly added server recovery tests also pass separately.
scenarios: Register invoice and edit before payment
Partial payment followed by full payment
Edit amounts, redistribute and unlink allocations
Reject invoice reduction below paid/reserved amounts
Recover failed allocation, invoice, settlement and operation updates
Verify settlement membership, signed totals, status rules, duplicate protection and currency guards

remaining_verification_and_decisions: No real financial records were created or edited for validation. Deluge compilation, hosted widget behavior and end-to-end CRM effects remain unverified.

Cross-record CRM writes are not an atomic transaction. Browser locks and unique operation keys protect same-operation retries; conditional writes detect many conflicts but do not provide global serialization across different users, external integrations and workflows. Simultaneous distinct payments against one invoice still require a shared server-side locking policy across every writer before claiming strict concurrency guarantees.

A complete live workflow/blueprint/external-integration inventory was not available. Two guessed legacy calculation function API names returned INVALID_DATA. Review delayed automation against the sources before production activation.
The complete formula expression for Unpaid_Invoiced_Amount was not exposed by field metadata. Widget calculations use payable minus paid; verify CRM reports and formula semantics separately.

Retained the existing policy that editing allocations changes the recorded payment amount. Supporting bank payments with unapplied remainders needs an explicit business rule and corresponding accounting treatment.
Mixed-currency allocations are blocked rather than inventing exchange conversion rules. Existing currency and rates are not rewritten.
External callers of createSupplierPaymentFromInvoices must supply a stable operation_key and explicit allocations. Review integrations outside this repository before deployment.

Recovery journals are browser-local, not a cross-device transaction ledger. Do not clear browser storage during an unfinished operation; after storage loss review existing unique-key records before retrying manually.
